podcast-tuckercarlson-3EAYlgYB2ko:
Tucker Carlson devotes this episode to the deep past as his guests and sources describe it. The subjects include giants in old accounts and the pyramids of Egypt. They also include the CIA's documented experiments with psychic spies, and civilizations said to be more advanced than the modern world before some great fall.

Each topic has a paper trail of some kind, from declassified remote-viewing files to nineteenth-century newspaper reports of giant skeletons. Carlson treats them as pieces of one suppressed history. The claims vary widely in support, and the episode moves by suggestion as much as by proof. It is preserved as a specimen of a popular genre: alternative history argued at length for a mainstream-sized audience. Listeners can enjoy the tour while keeping their own tally of what is documented and what is not.
the-tragedy-of-the-korosko:
Arthur Conan Doyle opens The Tragedy of the Korosko by explaining why the public never read of it in the papers. Personal and political reasons held the story back, though versions leaked into a provincial paper and were discredited. Doyle says the narrative was collated from the sworn statements of Colonel Cochrane Cochrane and the letters of Miss Adams of Boston. Captain Archer of the Egyptian Camel Corps added evidence given before a secret inquiry at Cairo.

The Korosko herself, a turtle-bottomed stern-wheeler of thirty-inch draught, left Shellal on 13 February 1895 bound for Wady Halfa. Doyle prints her passenger card: colonels, Bostonians, a Frenchman, a Dublin couple, and a Birmingham clergyman. This documentary frame gives his Nile adventure the flavour of a suppressed scandal about to be told at last.
